comments.body:
Host inspection: the volume being unmounted is only half of it. **The declaration marker that would make gate admission REFUSE does not exist either**, so the fail-loud protection is inert rather than merely unarmed.

**Measured on the host, 2026-09-05 ~11:55 UTC** (read-only metadata only — I cancelled an earlier `du` when it ran long, given this host's documented IOPS-saturation history):

    $ mountpoint /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch
    /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch is not a mountpoint

    $ ls -la /var/lib/rebar/.gate-scratch-required
    ls: cannot access '/var/lib/rebar/.gate-scratch-required': No such file or directory

    $ ls /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch/
    rebar-gate-snapshots
    reviewbot-vnaa57x_
    semgrep-mcp
    tmpgvy_yxuz
    tmpqk2k1l2n.json

    $ lsblk
    nvme1n1   50G  xfs   /var/gerrit
    nvme0n1p1 60G  xfs   /
    nvme2n1   50G              <- the gate-scratch volume: attached, NO fstype, unmounted

So the directory is a plain directory on ROOT, and it is in ACTIVE USE — gate snapshots, a live review-bot clone, semgrep-mcp, and loose temp files are all landing on the root filesystem right now, which is the exact condition ADR 0112 created this volume to end.

**Why the refusal never fires, which is the part worth fixing.** `user_data.sh` writes two markers, and only AFTER a successful mount:

    touch "$GATE_SCRATCH_MOUNT/../.gate-scratch-required"   # DECLARATION, on ROOT, survives unmount
    touch "$GATE_SCRATCH_MOUNT/.gate-scratch-mounted"       # PROOF, on the VOLUME, disappears with it

and its own comment states the contract: *"Declaration present + proof absent => gate admission refuses instead of quietly repopulating the store on root."*

Both markers are absent. So the state gate admission actually observes is "no declaration" — which it reads as *this host has no dedicated scratch volume*, and proceeds on root without complaint. The design distinguishes three states but only defends against one of them:

- declaration + proof -> mounted, proceed. Correct.
- declaration, no proof -> volume vanished, REFUSE. Correct, and the case the design was built for.
- **no declaration -> assume no volume exists, proceed on root.** This host. Silent.

**The structural problem: the declaration can only be written by the thing that also does the mount.** `user_data.sh` runs at instance LAUNCH. This volume was attached by Terraform to an already-running instance, so that block has never executed here, and it cannot execute without an instance replacement. A host that acquires the volume after launch is therefore guaranteed to sit in the third state — the volume exists in AWS, Terraform believes it is provisioned, the alarm exists, and nothing on the box knows it is supposed to be there.

That is why this has been silent all night rather than loud. It is not that the guard failed; it is that the guard's precondition is written by the same one-shot path that was skipped.

**Consequences for the remediation plan.** Mounting alone is not sufficient and doing it naively makes things worse in one specific way: the live contents listed above sit AT the mount point, so mounting over them SHADOWS them — they keep consuming root while becoming invisible to `du` and to every read-only probe. That is very likely a contributor to the unattributed ~21 GB recorded on `cyclopean-bloodshot-hoatzin` (du accounts 21.24 GB where df says 42.4 GB), whose leading hypothesis was exactly "files shadowed under mount points".

So the sequence has to be: quiesce the consumers, MOVE the existing contents off the path (not just mount over them), mount, write BOTH markers, then verify `mountpoint` succeeds and gate admission sees declaration+proof. Writing `.gate-scratch-required` at any earlier point would arm the refusal against a host that cannot yet satisfy it and would block every gate on the box.

Worth considering as a follow-up rather than here: the declaration ought to be derivable from something that survives a post-launch volume attach — the Terraform-known volume id, or a systemd unit that reconciles markers on boot — so that "the volume was added after launch" stops being a silent state.

comments.body:
## Re-verified on the live host 2026-09-05 ~22:24 UTC (read-only SSM) — and ONE FIGURE HAS MOVED MATERIALLY

Everything in this ticket's description still holds, with one exception that changes the urgency.

```
lsblk -o NAME,SIZE,FSTYPE,MOUNTPOINT,SERIAL
  nvme1n1        50G xfs    /var/gerrit   vol06fa2e77a9dd97527
  nvme0n1        60G                      vol0270fcf13709cf472
  ├─nvme0n1p1    60G xfs    /
  └─nvme0n1p128  10M vfat   /boot/efi
  nvme2n1        50G   ---     ---        vol06780b8557d1416b7   <- still raw, still unmounted

blkid /dev/nvme2n1                       -> NO FILESYSTEM
/etc/fstab                               -> /, /boot/efi, /var/gerrit ONLY. No gate-scratch line.
mountpoint /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch   -> is not a mountpoint
.gate-scratch-required                   -> No such file or directory
.gate-scratch-mounted                    -> No such file or directory
```

Live contents, mtimes at the moment of inspection (22:21-22:24), i.e. **being written right now**:
`rebar-gate-snapshots` (203 entries), `reviewbot-r7x216ij`, `semgrep-mcp`, and five loose
`tmp*` files.

**THE CHANGE — root has gone from 57% to 81%.**

```
                 ticket (earlier)      now
  df -h /        34G / 60G  (57%)      49G / 60G  (81%)   12G free
  df -h /var/gerrit                    11G / 50G  (21%)
```

Root has gained roughly **15G in about eleven hours** while gate scratch runs on it. The ticket's
"stable, which is why this is not a p1" assessment was true when written and is weaker now: at this
rate the margin is days, not weeks, and a full root takes Gerrit down with it — the exact coupling
S1 removed on paper. I am not re-prioritising the ticket unilaterally, but an operator deciding
when to take the quiet window should weigh 12G free, not 26G.

## Two findings that change the remediation sequence

**1. A `du` over this directory does not complete in a usable time.** I started a read-only
`du -sh --one-file-system` on the scratch tree at 22:30 UTC; it had not returned after **25
minutes**, so I cancelled it rather than add load to a host with documented IOPS saturation. So I
did NOT re-measure the 9.3G figure, and I do not trust it as current given root grew 15G. The
practical consequence: **the remediation must not depend on `du`** — every space check should use
`df`, which is O(1). The runbook I am writing does exactly that.

**2. The review-bot container binds the PARENT, so a host mount will not reach it.**
`infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:305` binds `/var/lib/rebar:/var/lib/rebar`, not the mount point
(deliberately — the comment there explains that binding only the mount point would make the
declaration marker invisible and the guard unable to fire). Docker bind mounts default to
`rprivate` propagation, so **a mount created on the host UNDERNEATH that existing bind does not
appear inside the already-running container.**

That means an operator who quiesces, mounts, writes the markers and then merely `docker compose
start review-bot` gets a split brain: the host shows a correctly mounted, empty volume and every
host-side check says "fixed", while the bot keeps writing to the OLD root directory through its
pre-existing bind. **`docker compose up -d --force-recreate review-bot` is mandatory, not tidiness.**
This is not stated anywhere in the ticket or in `review-bot-ops.md`, and it is the single most
likely way this remediation gets declared done while remaining in effect.

Nothing was mutated: read-only inspection only, and my one long-running probe was cancelled.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## Deliverables, and the boundary I did not cross

**Nothing on the host or in AWS was mutated.** No format, no mount, no fstab edit, no data move,
no `terraform apply`, no service restart. Terraform was read-only throughout (`-lock=false`, so
not even the S3 state lock was written). The one long-running probe I started was cancelled
rather than left to load an IOPS-starved host.

### Deliverable 1 — `infra/runbooks/gate-scratch-mount.md`

A turnkey procedure for a RUNNING host, grounded in what was measured over SSM rather than in
what `user_data.sh` does at launch. Eleven sections; every action carries its own verification
(with the expected output) and its own rollback, and the point of no return is named.

Three things in it are not in this ticket and are the reason a naive sequence fails:

1. **Move the contents aside; do not mount over them.** A rename on the same filesystem is
   atomic and instant, leaves the mount point empty so nothing is ever shadowed, and turns the
   rollback into a second rename. Mounting over live scratch instead hides those inodes while
   processes keep writing to them, so the space is never reclaimed and is invisible to `du` --
   very likely a contributor to the unattributed ~21 GB on `cyclopean-bloodshot-hoatzin`.
2. **The container recreate is mandatory.** `docker-compose.yml:305` binds `/var/lib/rebar`, the
   PARENT, and Docker binds default to `rprivate` propagation, so a host mount created under a
   running container does not appear inside it. An operator who mounts and merely restarts gets
   a split brain in which every host-side check reads healthy while the bot still writes to the
   old root directory. The plan-review gate independently found this too, which is some
   corroboration that it is real and not a private theory.
3. **Markers proof-first**, diverging deliberately from `user_data.sh:237-238`'s
   declaration-first order. That script runs pre-service at boot when no gate can be admitted,
   so its window is empty; on a live host, writing the declaration first refuses every gate on
   the box until the proof lands. `chmod 0700` precedes both (bug `ad8d` AC3).

It also never uses `du`, because a read-only `du -sh` over this tree did not return in 25
minutes and had to be cancelled -- so every space check is `df`, which is O(1). A consequence
worth stating: **the 9.3G figure was NOT re-measured and should not be trusted as current**,
given root grew ~15G in the same window.

### Deliverable 2 — `scripts/assert_volumes_in_service.py` (AC5, the delivery gap)

Terraform holds one half of the answer -- which volumes are attached -- and the host holds the
other -- which mount points are backed by a real filesystem. Neither is wrong alone; nothing
joined them. This performs that join and fails loudly, naming the volume and pointing at the
runbook, so "delivered but not in effect" is an error at apply time rather than an alarm noticed
days later. Three outcomes, not two: `UNKNOWN` (the host did not report the device) stays
distinct from `NOT-IN-SERVICE` and also fails, because "I could not tell" must not read as "it
is fine" -- the same conflation shape as the bug itself.

Two alternatives were considered and REJECTED, with reasons recorded in the module docstring so
they are not re-litigated:

- **A post-boot auto-reconciler cannot cover this case.** Auto-mounting an already-formatted
  volume is safe; this volume was RAW, and auto-`mkfs` on a volume that merely looks blank is
  how a restored backup gets destroyed. The unsafe half is exactly the half that was needed.
- **Flipping `rebar.llm.gate_admission` to refuse on a missing declaration is a real design
  change**, not a bug fix: the marker pair is deliberately opt-in by provisioning so no laptop
  or CI runner changes behaviour on upgrade, and landing the flip while this volume is still
  unmounted would refuse every gate on the box. Filed as `reportable-commutual-rooster`
  (`1064-8c4a-f399-41de`), linked `discovered_from`, and sequenced explicitly AFTER the runbook
  is executed.

RED-first and perturbation-checked: the headline test reproduces the ACTUAL production state
from the measured serials and requires it to fail; treating an unmounted volume as in-service
turns that test red, and dropping the dashless-serial normalisation turns three red including
the passing case (without it every volume silently becomes `UNKNOWN` -- a guard that fails for
the wrong reason). 9 tests, offline, no AWS.

### What I did NOT establish

- Whether the current on-root scratch is still ~9.3G. The `du` did not complete.
- Anything about how the host behaves AFTER the mount: no step of the runbook has been executed,
  so its verifications are predictions grounded in measured state, not observations.
- Whether the review-bot has other writers of `/var/lib/rebar` beyond the compose service and
  host-side `rebar` gate runs. I confirmed the compose bind is the only one in
  `docker-compose.yml`; I did not enumerate host processes (`lsof` was not run).

comments.body:
## The host REBOOTED at ~23:52 UTC, and it changes three things — measured, read-only

Gerrit went unreachable (`curl` refused on :443, `git ls-remote` reset). SSM showed `up 0 min`.
It is back now. Three consequences, all verified rather than inferred:

### 1. The remediation is STILL required, and the reboot did not help

```
lsblk   nvme1n1  50G xfs  /var/gerrit  vol06fa2e77a9dd97527
        nvme2n1  50G  --      --       vol06780b8557d1416b7   <- still raw, still unmounted
/etc/fstab                -> still no gate-scratch line
.gate-scratch-required    -> still absent
.gate-scratch-mounted     -> still absent
mountpoint gate-scratch   -> is not a mountpoint
```

This is the expected behaviour and it is worth stating plainly, because "have you tried
rebooting it" is the obvious wrong idea here: **cloud-init runs user-data ONCE PER INSTANCE, not
once per boot.** A reboot does not re-run `user_data.sh`, so it cannot format or mount a volume
attached after first boot, and it did not. Only an instance REPLACEMENT would — at the cost of
replacing the production Gerrit host. This reboot is therefore a direct empirical confirmation of
the mechanism this ticket describes, rather than a coincidence.

### 2. Root fell from 81% to 76% — relief, not resolution

```
before reboot   49G of 60G (81%), 12G free
after  reboot   46G of 60G (76%), 15G free
```

~3G of transient files went with the restart (the per-review `reviewbot-*` clones are gone;
`rebar-gate-snapshots`, `semgrep-mcp` and the loose `tmp*` files survived). The trend that took
root from 57% to 81% in eleven hours is unchanged — this bought hours, not a fix.

### 3. DEVICE NAMES ARE NOT A SAFE IDENTIFIER, and I now have a direct observation

At `up 0 min`, `df -h` reported:

```
/dev/nvme2n1     50G   11G   40G  21% /var/gerrit
```

One minute later `lsblk` reported `nvme1n1 ... /var/gerrit` and `nvme2n1` as the unmounted
gate-scratch volume — the original mapping. So the two reads DISAGREED about which device node
backs `/var/gerrit`, a minute apart, on the same host. Most likely the first was taken while NVMe
enumeration was still settling.

**Why this matters more than a curiosity.** `/var/gerrit` is Gerrit's data volume, and it is
mounted by UUID, so it followed its filesystem correctly and nothing was harmed. But the
remediation for THIS ticket runs `mkfs.xfs` on the gate-scratch device. An operator who had
copied `/dev/nvme2n1` out of an earlier note and run `mkfs.xfs /dev/nvme2n1` during that window
would have **formatted Gerrit's data volume.**

`infra/runbooks/gate-scratch-mount.md` already refuses that, in two independent ways, and I am
recording this because the reboot turned a defensive precaution into a demonstrated one:

- §0 and §4 both re-confirm the target by **SERIAL** (`vol06780b8557d1416b7`), never by device
  name, and §5 writes fstab by **UUID** for the same reason.
- §4 will not format at all unless `blkid` reports NO filesystem — so even a mis-identified
  device that already carries xfs is refused rather than overwritten.

No action is required from this comment. Nothing was mutated; every command above was read-only.

compiled_state.description:
## The finding

Epic 6202's story **S1 (`aa40-cbda`) is CLOSED, but its deliverable is not in effect.** The
gate-scratch volume exists, is attached, and is raw and unmounted; gate scratch runs on the ROOT
filesystem -- precisely the silent fallback S1 exists to prevent.

## Measured on the live host (SSM, read-only)

```
lsblk    nvme2n1  50G  no FSTYPE, no MOUNTPOINT   serial vol06780b8557d1416b7
blkid /dev/nvme2n1        -> no filesystem at all
/etc/fstab                -> /, /boot/efi, /var/gerrit ONLY; no gate-scratch line
mountpoint gate-scratch   -> is not a mountpoint
.gate-scratch-required    -> ABSENT      .gate-scratch-mounted -> ABSENT
df -h /                   -> 49G of 60G (81%) as of 2026-09-05 22:24 UTC
```

AWS confirms the volume is `in-use`, attached to `i-00880b2c7f13527c5` at `/dev/sdg`, with a
matching NVMe serial -- so there is no ambiguity about which device it is. It simply was never
formatted or mounted. **Root has grown from 57% to 81%**; see the re-verification comment for the
current reading and two findings that change the remediation sequence.

## Why it happened

The volume was created by a `terraform apply` AFTER the instance's first boot. `user_data.sh`
runs under cloud-init on FIRST BOOT ONLY, so its `mount_ebs_volume "${gate_scratch_volume_id}"`
step has never executed for this volume, and nothing else on the host mounts it. The script is
correct; it simply never ran. That is a gap in the delivery path, not a logic bug.

## The monitoring worked -- and is worth crediting

Both alarms are correctly in ALARM. `rebar-gate-scratch-unmounted` reads `gate_scratch_mounted`
= 0. `rebar-gate-scratch-disk-high` publishes NOTHING (no mount to `df`) and, because
`treat_missing_data = "breaching"`, alarms rather than reading healthy -- the dead-man-correct
behaviour `bff5-9163` was closed for. So this WAS detectable and detected. What was missing is
that S1 closed on code correctness without a check that the volume entered service.

## Why this is DEGRADED, not BROKEN, and why remediation is not a simple mount

`user_data.sh:236-238` writes two markers to deliberately different filesystems (`chmod 0700` at
`:236`, declaration `:237`, proof `:238`; contract in the comment at `:222-228`). The range this
ticket first cited, `:123-130`, is the device-resolution `readlink -f` branch from bug `ad8d` F5
and has nothing to do with markers. `.gate-scratch-required` sits beside the mount point on ROOT
(surviving an unmount); `.gate-scratch-mounted` sits inside it on the VOLUME. Declaration present
+ proof absent makes gate admission REFUSE rather than repopulate on root.

Here BOTH are absent, so admission reads "this host has no dedicated volume" and gates run on
root. Stable, hence not p1 -- but the isolation S1 bought is not being had, and a gate run that
fills root now takes Gerrit down with it.

`/var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch` holds LIVE, in-use working directories. Mounting over them HIDES
them from any process that opens them afterwards while stranding the bytes on root, and doing it
mid-review breaks that run. The contents are genuinely scratch, so nothing needs migrating -- but
a quiet window does, and the stranded copy must be removed or the space is lost twice. The full
ordered procedure -- quiesce, MOVE the contents aside (never mount over them), format,
fstab-by-UUID, mount, assert `mountpoint -q` BEFORE any marker, write the markers proof-first,
RECREATE the review-bot container, reclaim, then confirm from CloudWatch -- lives in
`infra/runbooks/gate-scratch-mount.md`, with a verification and a rollback per step. Do not
improvise from this summary.

## Scope split: what lands in code, and what only an operator can do

AC1-AC4 and AC6 are HOST actions on a running production box. No agent performs them, so they
are tagged `[non-codebase]` and are discharged by an operator executing
`infra/runbooks/gate-scratch-mount.md` and recording the result here. What lands as code is that
runbook plus AC5/AC7's delivery-gap assertion. That is not a descope: for AC1-AC4 the risky part
is the SEQUENCE, so a turnkey, verified, rollback-per-step procedure IS the deliverable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] [non-codebase] The gate-scratch volume is formatted, in `/etc/fstab` by UUID, and mounted at
      `/var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch`. Proven by `mountpoint -q` and `lsblk` showing the fstype.
- [ ] [non-codebase] Both markers exist on their intended filesystems, created in the safe order, and
      `chmod 0700` is applied. Proven by `ls` plus confirming they are on different devices.
- [ ] [non-codebase] `rebar/host:gate_scratch_mounted` publishes 1 and `disk_used_percent` resumes publishing;
      both alarms return to OK. Proven from CloudWatch, not from the host alone.
- [ ] [non-codebase] The stranded copy under root is reclaimed and `df /` reflects it.
- [ ] AC5 (the only NON-`[non-codebase]` criterion). Concrete edit target:
      **`scripts/assert_volumes_in_service.py`** (new) with its offline oracle
      `tests/unit/test_assert_volumes_in_service_dcc3.py` (new). It joins the two halves nobody
      had joined -- terraform's `aws_volume_attachment` set against the host's mount table --
      and fails, naming the volume, when one is attached but not in service. Three outcomes,
      not two: `UNKNOWN` (the host did not report the device) stays distinct from
      `NOT-IN-SERVICE` and also fails. Flipping `rebar.llm.gate_admission` to refuse on a
      missing declaration would refuse every gate on this box while it is unmounted; filed as
      `reportable-commutual-rooster` (`1064-8c4a-f399-41de`).
- [ ] [non-codebase] The review-bot container is RECREATED after the host mount, and the mount is
      verified FROM INSIDE it. `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:305` binds `/var/lib/rebar` —
      the PARENT — and Docker binds default to `rprivate` propagation, so a mount created on the
      host underneath a running container does NOT appear inside it. Without this the bot keeps
      writing to the shadowed pre-mount directory while every host-side check reads healthy.
      Proven by `docker compose exec review-bot sh -c 'stat -c %D /var/lib/rebar/gate-scratch;
      stat -c %D /var/lib/rebar'` returning TWO DIFFERENT device ids, and by
      `.gate-scratch-mounted` being visible inside the container.
- [ ] AC7 -- the delivery gap is closed as a CLASS, and ONE mechanism is CHOSEN rather than
      left as an either/or. **Chosen: the apply-time signal, not a post-boot reconciler.**
      Positive rationale, not elimination: a reconciler could safely auto-MOUNT an already
      formatted volume, but this one was RAW, and auto-`mkfs` on a volume that merely looks
      blank is how a restored backup is destroyed -- so that branch cannot cover the case that
      actually occurred, and a half-covering automation is worse than an honest check.
      **Invocation point, stated:** `scripts/assert_volumes_in_service.py` is a MANDATORY
      post-apply step, invoked from `infra/runbooks/gate-scratch-mount.md` §10 after this
      remediation and after ANY future `terraform apply` that adds or replaces a volume.
      Operation-linked deliberately, rather than bound to one CI provider, which is what
      `project.portability` requires.
      **Why it is not ALSO wired into `terraform-drift.yml`**, as a checkable fact rather than
      an omission: that workflow assumes the `rebar-terraform-plan` OIDC role, which is
      `ReadOnlyAccess` + `kms:Decrypt` (`infra/terraform/iam.tf:178-191`). `ssm:SendCommand` is
      a WRITE action absent from `ReadOnlyAccess`, so that role cannot run the host probe at
      all. Granting it is an IAM widening with its own blast radius and needs its own ticket.
      A fix that only mounts this one volume by hand would leave the next to be found the same
      way -- by an alarm, days later.

file_impact.reason: AC1-AC4: the turnkey operator procedure for putting the already-attached, still-raw gate-scratch volume into service on a RUNNING host -- quiesce, move-aside (never mount over live scratch), format, fstab-by-UUID, mount, markers in the safe order on their two filesystems, mandatory container recreate, reclaim, and CloudWatch confirmation, each step with its own verification and rollback

cross-reference: its existing 'volume is not mounted' recovery assumes an fstab entry exists and `mount -a` suffices, which is false for a volume attached after first boot; point that case at the new runbook instead of letting an operator improvise from it

AC5 delivery gap: a post-apply assertion that every EBS volume terraform attaches to the instance is actually IN SERVICE on the host, so 'declared but never mounted' becomes a loud, actionable failure at apply time instead of a per-volume alarm someone must have remembered to write
AC5 oracle: offline tests of the classification logic (attached+mounted, attached+unmounted, unknown) plus defect seeding to prove the assertion is load-bearing

compiled_state.title: Epic 6202 S1 closed but its deliverable never entered service: the gate-scratch EBS volume is attached, RAW and unmounted, and gate scratch has been running on the root filesystem
